title: Vesta
subtitle: The giant asteroid
yt_title: This Asteroid Has a 22 km Mountain ☄️ | Ep. 99 #shorts
description:
Episode 99 of a daily journey through the universe. ☄️
We visit Vesta, one of the biggest asteroids: about 525 km wide, a giant impact basin with a central peak about 22 km tall, pieces that fell to Earth as meteorites, and NASA's Dawn spacecraft that orbited it in 2011–2012.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 100: Next stop, Kepler-452b. Earth's older cousin?

Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

segments.text: Between Mars and Jupiter lies the asteroid belt. And one of its giants is Vesta.
segments.headline: A giant asteroid

segments.text: It's about five hundred and twenty-five kilometers wide. Big enough that you can sometimes see it without a telescope.
Long ago, something huge slammed into its south pole, leaving a crater almost as wide as Vesta itself.
segments.headline: A giant impact

segments.text: In the middle of that crater stands a mountain about twenty-two kilometers tall. More than twice the height of Everest.
That impact blasted pieces into space. Some of them fell on Earth. About one in every twenty meteorites found here came from Vesta.
segments.headline: Vesta on Earth

segments.text: Inside, Vesta has a metal core, a mantle and a crust, just like a small planet. It almost became one.
segments.headline: An almost planet

segments.text: NASA's Dawn spacecraft orbited Vesta from twenty eleven to twenty twelve, then flew on to the dwarf planet Ceres.
segments.headline: Dawn's visit

segments.text: Vesta is a time capsule from when the planets were being built, four and a half billion years ago.
segments.headline: A time capsule

segments.text: Tomorrow, episode one hundred! We leave the solar system to visit a planet called Earth's older cousin. Follow, so you don't miss it.
